name: Punctuation and conjunction clauses
hypothesis: Independent clauses retrieve evidence that a long compound query can dilute.
mechanism: Split on sentence punctuation, semicolons, newlines, and major conjunctions.
limitation: Conjunctions inside a single concept can be split incorrectly.

name: Enumeration items
hypothesis: Searching list members separately reduces competition among enumerated terms.
mechanism: Detect comma, semicolon, or ideographic-comma lists and emit each item.
limitation: Ordinary comma-separated prose can look like an enumeration.

name: Quoted phrase islands
hypothesis: Quoted text often names the exact phrase that should match memory.
mechanism: Emit spans inside straight or typographic quotation marks.
limitation: Quotations used for emphasis may not be retrieval entities.

name: Parenthetical dual view
hypothesis: Main text and parenthetical qualifiers may match different source wording.
mechanism: Emit the query without bracketed text and each bracketed span separately.
limitation: Nested or unmatched brackets are intentionally not parsed.

name: Named-entity islands
hypothesis: Capitalized, acronym, and alphanumeric spans provide high-precision anchors.
mechanism: Extract consecutive entity-like Latin tokens without an external entity model.
limitation: Sentence-initial capitalization can create false entities.
manual_review: Only improved validation case adds first-person I as entity alias; mechanism hypothesis unsupported. Used-data regression negative.

name: Relation-centered propositions
hypothesis: Subject-relation-object fragments preserve relational intent in shorter queries.
mechanism: Extract bounded token windows around common temporal and semantic relations.
limitation: The fixed relation vocabulary misses implicit and uncommon relations.

name: Interrogative core
hypothesis: Removing a leading question scaffold makes content terms dominate lexical search.
mechanism: Strip a bounded leading wh-question phrase while retaining the original query.
limitation: Complex inversion can leave an incomplete or ungrammatical core.

name: Temporal anchors
hypothesis: Dates and relative periods can independently recover time-specific evidence.
mechanism: Extract years, month-year forms, quarters, and simple relative periods.
limitation: A time expression alone can retrieve unrelated events from the same period.

name: Contrast branches
hypothesis: Searching both sides of an explicit contrast can recover evidence for either choice.
mechanism: Split once on versus, rather than, instead of, or but not.
limitation: The two branches may depend on shared context lost by the split.

name: Corpus-rare term islands
hypothesis: High-IDF query terms can recover precise evidence hidden by common words.
mechanism: Emit up to four unique query tokens ordered by corpus IDF and source position.
limitation: Rare misspellings and identifiers can receive misleading priority.

name: Unicode compatibility form
hypothesis: Compatibility-equivalent characters should share lexical matches.
mechanism: Add an NFKC-normalized query for width, ligature, and compatibility forms.
limitation: NFKC can erase distinctions that are meaningful in specialized notation.

name: Unicode case folding
hypothesis: Multi-character case folds can match spellings outside baseline lowercasing.
mechanism: Add Unicode casefold aliases, such as sharp-s to ss, beyond simple lowercasing.
limitation: Case can distinguish identifiers and proper names.

name: Cardinal word-number aliases
hypothesis: Explicit number words can recover numeric evidence and vice versa.
mechanism: Exchange standalone English cardinal words and decimal integers from 0 to 99.
limitation: Larger numbers are not expanded; number words can have nonnumeric meanings.

name: Hyphen topology aliases
hypothesis: Hyphenated, spaced, and joined forms often describe the same lexical item.
mechanism: Canonicalize dash characters and add spaced and joined word forms.
limitation: Changing a hyphen can merge terms whose punctuation is meaningful.

name: Possessive aliases
hypothesis: Possessive punctuation differences should not block a noun match.
mechanism: Canonicalize apostrophes and add a form without English possessive suffixes.
limitation: The pattern cannot reliably distinguish every possessive from a contraction.

name: Acronym punctuation
hypothesis: Dotted and letter-spaced acronyms should match compact acronym forms.
mechanism: Compact repeated single-letter acronym forms without a dictionary.
limitation: Ordinary isolated capital letters can be mistaken for an acronym.

name: Identifier segmentation
hypothesis: Splitting identifier boundaries exposes words hidden in code-like names.
mechanism: Split camel case, acronym transitions, separators, and letter-digit boundaries.
limitation: Opaque hashes and product identifiers may become noisy fragments.

name: Numeric grouping marks
hypothesis: Grouped and ungrouped digit strings should retrieve the same numeric evidence.
mechanism: Remove comma or underscore grouping marks before three-digit groups.
limitation: Locale-specific decimal commas can be misread as grouping marks.

name: Source-defined abbreviation expansion
hypothesis: An explicitly defined abbreviation can recover evidence using its full name.
mechanism: Expand initialisms from source-only long name (ABC) or ABC (long name) definitions.
limitation: Only parenthetical Latin initialisms are parsed; conflicting definitions are skipped.

name: Symbol word aliases
hypothesis: Textual names for common symbols can match prose that omits the glyph.
mechanism: Replace ampersand, plus, at, and percent symbols with generic word aliases.
limitation: Symbols can carry domain-specific meanings not captured by these words.

name: Message role labels
hypothesis: Indexing source roles improves retrieval of speaker-qualified requests.
mechanism: Append the original message role to index text and context without indexing IDs.
limitation: Roles do not identify a real person; role-neutral queries may gain irrelevant matches.

name: Heading path inheritance
hypothesis: Local heading paths recover chunks whose topic appears only in a section title.
mechanism: Inherit the active Markdown heading ancestry at each source span.
limitation: Only explicit Markdown headings are recognized; large sections can supply noisy context.

name: Explicit date aliases
hypothesis: Equivalent numeric and written dates match more consistently after index normalization.
mechanism: Add validated ISO or English month-name aliases for explicit dates in the span.
limitation: Ambiguous numeric dates, relative dates, other languages and implicit timestamps stay unchanged.

name: Negation cue indexing
hypothesis: Repeating marked negative clauses increases recall for negative-constraint requests.
mechanism: Index literal English negative markers and their original clause with descriptive labels.
limitation: Markers do not establish semantic scope; quotations and double negatives remain ambiguous.

name: Identifier word indexing
hypothesis: Splitting source identifiers lets ordinary word queries find technical facts.
mechanism: Append lexical parts of camel case, acronym case, digit transitions and delimited identifiers.
limitation: Splits can be semantically wrong and do not supply synonyms or domain knowledge.

name: Field key inheritance
hypothesis: Clipped values become retrievable when their explicit field key is indexed with them.
mechanism: Attach a same-line key only to spans intersecting that key's value.
limitation: Only simple colon or equals fields are recognized; multiline and nested values are not parsed.

name: List ancestor inheritance
hypothesis: Nested list facts become retrievable by their otherwise missing parent labels.
mechanism: Attach original enclosing bullet labels using indentation within the same message.
limitation: Indentation is heuristic; malformed lists and distant prose can obscure parent boundaries.

name: Inline speaker inheritance
hypothesis: Chunks within explicit transcript turns match speaker-qualified requests more often.
mechanism: Attach the nearest explicit speaker header within the current nonblank transcript block.
limitation: Capitalized field keys can resemble names; blank lines end attribution conservatively.

name: Character fragment indexing
hypothesis: Character trigrams recover lexical partial matches absent from whole-token indexing.
mechanism: Append deduplicated source-word trigrams without changing source text or boundaries.
limitation: Shared fragments can increase false matches; short words and semantic paraphrases gain nothing.

name: Local acronym expansion
hypothesis: An explicit earlier long form makes later acronym-only chunks findable by expansion words.
mechanism: Reuse same-message parenthesized definitions whose long-form initials match the acronym.
limitation: Only explicit Latin initialisms are supported; definitions in other messages are not imported.

name: Sentence units
hypothesis: Punctuation-delimited facts reduce unrelated terms within retrieval candidates.
mechanism: Partition at sentence terminals with conservative English abbreviation and decimal handling.
limitation: Heuristic punctuation cannot reliably parse all abbreviations, code or unpunctuated speech.

name: Paragraph units
hypothesis: Blank-line paragraphs retain local context while separating unrelated discussion.
mechanism: Partition at blank lines, preserving single-newline continuations.
limitation: A paragraph may mix topics; unformatted messages remain at baseline segmentation.

name: Heading sections
hypothesis: Keeping each explicit heading with its section preserves topic-to-fact locality.
mechanism: Partition on ATX and setext headings outside fenced code.
limitation: Nested headings start new sections; long sections are not subdivided by size.

name: Hierarchical list items
hypothesis: Keeping nested bullets with their root item preserves dependencies in enumerated facts.
mechanism: Partition root-level list items and surrounding prose, retaining nested children.
limitation: Malformed indentation and lazy unindented continuations can create false boundaries.

name: Markdown table rows
hypothesis: Row units isolate structured records that baseline chunks can mix together.
mechanism: Detect header-divider tables; keep the header with the first row and split later rows.
limitation: Later rows do not inherit headers; multiline cells and irregular column counts are unsupported.

name: Transcript turns
hypothesis: Explicit speaker turns keep attribution attached to each utterance.
mechanism: Partition messages with at least two line-start speaker headers outside code.
limitation: Capitalized field keys may resemble speakers; unlabeled dialogue stays unchanged.

name: Repeated-field records
hypothesis: Record boundaries prevent fields from adjacent entities sharing a candidate.
mechanism: Start a new record when a field key repeats within a contiguous key-value block.
limitation: Repeated keys inside one record can over-split; unique-key and nested records are ambiguous.

name: Atomic fenced blocks
hypothesis: Keeping fenced code intact preserves syntax and separates code from prose retrieval noise.
mechanism: Partition on matching Markdown code fences, retaining delimiters and complete code bodies.
limitation: Indented code is not recognized; an unclosed fence consumes the remaining message.

name: Explicit quotation blocks
hypothesis: Separating marked quotations reduces mixing of quoted claims with surrounding commentary.
mechanism: Partition greater-than-prefixed quote blocks outside code fences from surrounding prose.
limitation: Unmarked lazy continuation and natural-language quotation marks are not resolved.

name: Timestamped log events
hypothesis: Log events keep a timestamped event with its multiline details while separating neighbors.
mechanism: Partition at validated line-start ISO date-time or clock-time log prefixes.
limitation: Dates without times and nonstandard timestamps stay unchanged; clock order is not inferred.

name: Session aggregate support
hypothesis: Several independent hits in one session can be stronger evidence than one isolated hit.
mechanism: Add a bounded reciprocal-rank session support score to each baseline hit.
limitation: A long session with repeated wording can still accumulate excess support.

name: Session query coverage
hypothesis: Joint coverage of distinct query concepts identifies useful multi-turn sessions.
mechanism: Measure IDF-weighted query-term coverage across bounded documents in candidate sessions.
limitation: Lexical coverage does not resolve synonyms or implicit references.

name: Independent message support
hypothesis: Evidence from separate source messages is more useful than duplicate chunks.
mechanism: Aggregate only the best hit from each source message before boosting its session.
limitation: Repeated facts in genuinely distinct messages may still dominate.

name: Top-session reacquisition
hypothesis: A strong session can contain relevant chunks missed by the initial lexical top set.
mechanism: Rescore bounded documents from the six strongest candidate sessions by query-term IDF overlap.
limitation: Only lexically overlapping chunks in already discovered sessions can be acquired.

name: Session marginal coverage
hypothesis: Sessions covering different query concepts provide more complete evidence.
mechanism: Greedily promote session representatives with the largest uncovered IDF-weighted query coverage.
limitation: Coverage relies on exact tokens and can promote a merely incidental mention.

name: Session MMR
hypothesis: Token-diverse sessions provide broader evidence than near-duplicate conversations.
mechanism: Order session representatives by aggregate relevance minus source-token redundancy.
limitation: Lexically different sessions can describe the same event and receive too much diversity credit.

name: Complementary message siblings
hypothesis: A matched chunk's parent message can contain missing query concepts in other chunks.
mechanism: Acquire bounded sibling chunks only when they contain query tokens missing from the seed.
limitation: Lexically implicit continuation and chunks beyond the per-message limit are missed.

name: Prompt parent
hypothesis: A matched answer is easier to interpret with its exact source prompt.
mechanism: For assistant hits, add the nearest preceding user message in the same request.
limitation: Multi-user-message requests may have a more distant logical parent.
manual_review: Two improved and one regressed; source coverage loss and exploratory interval includes zero.

name: Response child
hypothesis: A matched prompt should retrieve its exact assistant response.
mechanism: For user hits, add the first following assistant message in the same request.
limitation: Tool messages or multi-answer requests may break the simple user-to-assistant hierarchy.

name: Split-query session intersection
hypothesis: Separate query concepts can identify a session even when they occur in different turns.
mechanism: Intersect session sets from up to four rare-term lexical lookups and acquire their matching chunks.
limitation: A rare term with no literal match prevents acquisition; each lookup is capped at 100 hits.

name: Latest source timestamp first
hypothesis: Recent source records are better first candidates for current-state queries.
mechanism: For undated current-state questions, rank newer source records first.
limitation: All old sources remain; a record timestamp is not necessarily a fact date.

name: Historical intent chronology
hypothesis: Explicit history questions benefit from earliest evidence first.
mechanism: For historical wording only, order dated hits from oldest to newest.
limitation: Implicit historical intent is left unchanged.

name: As-of source cutoff
hypothesis: An explicit as-of date should prioritize evidence recorded by that date.
mechanism: Prioritize sources recorded by the cutoff, exclusive for explicit before.
limitation: Uses UTC calendar days of millisecond timestamps, not event times.

name: Exact body date alignment
hypothesis: A date written in both query and source is strong temporal evidence.
mechanism: Promote documents containing the same complete calendar date as the query.
limitation: Equivalent relative dates and paraphrased dates are not interpreted.

name: Calendar spelling query aliases
hypothesis: Equivalent explicit date spellings recover otherwise missing lexical hits.
mechanism: Keep original and focused queries and add four equivalent date spellings.
limitation: No aliases for incomplete, invalid, multiple, or relative dates.

name: Stated validity interval
hypothesis: A source-stated date range can answer point-in-time retrieval directly.
mechanism: Promote documents with a closed written date range covering the query date.
limitation: Open-ended or implicit ranges are not inferred.

name: Update language promotion
hypothesis: Current-state questions benefit from sources that explicitly describe a change.
mechanism: For current wording, promote source text with update or replacement language.
limitation: Update language without a date does not prove it is the newest state.

name: Negation counterpart retrieval
hypothesis: Showing both polarities reduces errors when stored statements conflict.
mechanism: Add one lexical source with opposite negation and strong topic overlap.
limitation: Lexical polarity cannot resolve which source is correct or newer.

name: Extractive change clause
hypothesis: The exact clause describing a change is safer than an unrelated full chunk.
mechanism: For current queries, emit all query-linked original change sentences.
limitation: Only an explicit same-sentence change is extracted; no pronoun resolution.

name: Nearest recorded date
hypothesis: Queries naming a date benefit from records captured closest to that date.
mechanism: Order timestamped sources by absolute distance from the explicit query date.
limitation: Temporal proximity alone does not establish topical relevance.

name: Source entity bridge
hypothesis: A name shared with a query-matched source can connect otherwise unmatched evidence.
mechanism: Join through up to six non-query capitalized names; reject high-fanout pivots.
limitation: Capitalization misses lowercase names and cannot distinguish homonyms. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Explicit alias chain
hypothesis: Source-stated aliases can connect a query name to differently named records.
mechanism: Walk at most two bidirectional explicit alias edges and acquire literal alias mentions.
limitation: Only explicit English alias syntax is recognized; conflicting aliases remain ambiguous. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Definition dependency chain
hypothesis: A definition can refer to another locally defined term needed to interpret it.
mechanism: Follow defined terms occurring in definition bodies for at most two directed steps.
limitation: Only explicit means, defined-as and refers-to clauses are supported, not inferred meaning. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Source reference chain
hypothesis: Explicit note and heading references connect evidence across source messages.
mechanism: Follow two source-written references to unique textual anchors, with cycle checks.
limitation: Unresolved or ambiguous anchors and references beyond the hop limit are skipped. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Structured attribute chain
hypothesis: A field value that names another record can connect subjects to indirect properties.
mechanism: Join subject.field:value or pipe-delimited records by exact value-to-subject keys.
limitation: Unstructured prose, nested values and more than two successive joins are unsupported. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: List membership bridge
hypothesis: A query-matched group heading can lead to separately described member items.
mechanism: Join up to eight short bullet or numbered members to exact source mentions.
limitation: Only local heading-list structure is used; nested and descriptive items can be missed. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Indirect question entity bridge
hypothesis: An entity supplied in a response can connect a question to a missing query facet.
mechanism: Use a request-local Q&A only as a bridge to an external entity-and-facet source.
limitation: Requires an explicit question, a named response entity and a missing lexical facet. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Shared resource bridge
hypothesis: Separate source mentions of the same resource can supply complementary facts.
mechanism: Join literal HTTP resource identities locally without dereferencing any address.
limitation: URLs with credentials or query strings are excluded; different paths stay separate. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Exact quotation bridge
hypothesis: A quoted passage can connect a matched discussion to its fuller source context.
mechanism: Join bounded quotations of four to twenty-four tokens to exact original substrings.
limitation: Literal overlap does not prove authorship; paraphrases and short quotations are missed. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Converging entity paths
hypothesis: Two independent entity paths can isolate evidence linking separate query facets.
mechanism: Require distinct names and source messages with complementary query coverage at a join.
limitation: Needs two explicit facets and shared names; a single valid path is intentionally ignored. Expansion caps sources at 6000, text at 2400 characters, additions at 64, and skips marked private or recognizable sensitive messages.

name: Unique query coverage
hypothesis: Distinct query terms improve ranking over repeated matches to one term.
mechanism: Rank by the fraction of distinct focused query tokens present in source text.
limitation: Ignores word order, negation, term frequency and semantic paraphrases.

name: Minimum term window
hypothesis: Nearby matching terms are more likely to describe the same fact.
mechanism: Rank by matched-term density in the shortest token window covering all matched terms.
limitation: A compact partial match can outrank a complete but dispersed match.

name: Rare term balance
hypothesis: Balanced support for rare query terms resists repetition of only common terms.
mechanism: Rank by the IDF-weighted harmonic mean of tf/(tf+1); missing terms score zero.
limitation: Requires every literal query token and can suppress useful partial evidence.

name: Adjacent query pairs
hypothesis: Preserving adjacent query token pairs reduces bag-of-words false matches.
mechanism: Rank by the fraction of distinct query bigrams occurring in source token order.
limitation: Different query pairs can occur in separate passages; paraphrases lose credit.

name: Ordered query subsequence
hypothesis: Query order helps even when modifiers separate matching source words.
mechanism: Rank by longest common subsequence length divided by focused query length.
limitation: Allows arbitrarily distant matches; O(query tokens times source tokens) work.

name: Explicit speaker attribution
hypothesis: An explicitly requested speaker role should precede other matching speakers.
mechanism: Prefer lexically matching hits with the single role named in an English attribution.
limitation: Narrow English grammar only; role metadata does not establish truth or authorship.

name: Weakest query facet
hypothesis: Balanced coverage of separate query clauses improves multi-condition ranking.
mechanism: Split explicit conjunctions and punctuation; rank by minimum per-facet coverage.
limitation: Conjunctions need not be independent facets; distributed evidence can be demoted.

name: Source lexical cosine
hypothesis: Length-normalized lexical focus reduces distracting long-document matches.
mechanism: Rank by TF-IDF cosine between focused query and the full original source text.
limitation: Can penalize useful context and qualifiers; exact repetitions are scale invariant.

name: Corpus background likelihood
hypothesis: Corpus-relative query likelihood separates informative matches from common wording.
mechanism: Use add-one corpus probabilities and Dirichlet mass equal to mean document length.
limitation: Lexical repetition is not proof; chunk overlap biases background token counts.

name: Single sentence support
hypothesis: Terms in one sentence are more useful than terms spread across unrelated sentences.
mechanism: Rank by maximum unique query-token coverage in any one source sentence.
limitation: Punctuation rules are approximate and do not resolve negation or clause meaning.

name: Exact text deduplication
hypothesis: Removing repeated text leaves more room for distinct evidence.
mechanism: Keep the first incoming hit for each exactly equal Python text string.
limitation: Identical statements at different times lose their separate event provenance.

name: Source overlap subtraction
hypothesis: Removing already presented source coordinates reduces overlapping chunk waste.
mechanism: Subtract earlier intervals within each source message and emit exact residual spans.
limitation: Residuals may start mid-word and lose context; distinct messages never coalesce.

name: Best supporting sentence
hypothesis: A sentence with maximal query coverage removes distracting surrounding text.
mechanism: Extract the earliest sentence with maximal distinct query-token coverage per hit.
limitation: May omit adjacent qualifiers; punctuation segmentation is approximate.

name: Best supporting paragraph
hypothesis: A source paragraph retains nearby explanations while removing unrelated paragraphs.
mechanism: Extract the earliest blank-line-delimited paragraph with maximal query coverage.
limitation: No compression without paragraph boundaries; other paragraphs may add needed context.

name: Shortest covering passage
hypothesis: A continuous passage can retain split support without the whole document.
mechanism: Extract the shortest sentence-aligned span covering all query terms matched in a hit.
limitation: A distant match forces a long passage; absent query terms remain absent.

name: Independent message support
hypothesis: Keeping distinct messages for each query term reduces repeated-chunk evidence.
mechanism: Keep the first two distinct message sources for each query token in incoming order.
limitation: Different messages can repeat a claim; a third message with new details may be lost.

name: Lexical evidence diversity
hypothesis: Lexically distinct evidence reduces repetition near the top of a ranked list.
mechanism: Maximize normalized input rank minus half maximum selected Jaccard similarity.
limitation: Lexical novelty can promote distractors; pairwise comparisons take quadratic time.

name: Chronological presentation
hypothesis: Source-time order makes changing statements easier to interpret.
mechanism: Order known timestamps ascending, then unknown timestamps, with source-order ties.
limitation: Old low-ranked evidence can displace useful recent evidence before top-k truncation.

name: Budgeted query coverage
hypothesis: New query terms per character can fit complementary evidence into a fixed budget.
mechanism: Select whole hits by new token coverage per character within 4096 code points.
limitation: Skips oversized hits and repeated corroboration; lexical coverage is not sufficiency.

name: Source message blocks
hypothesis: Restoring source fragment order improves reading of evidence from the same message.
mechanism: Group by opaque message ID in first-hit order, then sort each block by source offset.
limitation: Grouping can move low-ranked fragments ahead of stronger hits from another message.

name: Direct lexical evidence only
hypothesis: Returning only directly matched sources reduces unsupported disclosure.
mechanism: Keep hits sharing an informative query token; return no hits without support.
limitation: Synonyms and indirect references can cause false abstention.

name: Quoted evidence match
hypothesis: Quoted requests should disclose only sources containing the exact quoted text.
mechanism: When the query contains quotes, require every quoted span in the source text.
limitation: Paraphrases and normalized formatting do not count as exact support.

name: Same-message context gate
hypothesis: Context from the directly matched message is safer than unrelated expansion.
mechanism: Keep direct hits plus chunks sharing their source message; otherwise abstain.
limitation: Relevant context recorded in another message is excluded.

name: Requested speaker only
hypothesis: Explicit speaker questions should not expose another speaker's text.
mechanism: When the query names user or assistant speech, keep only that source role.
limitation: Ambiguous or unstated speaker intent leaves baseline results unchanged.

name: Sensitive category intent
hypothesis: Sensitive sources should appear only when the query requests that category.
mechanism: Require query intent for every sensitive category in each returned source.
limitation: English category keywords and numeric heuristics can miss or over-mark data.

name: Sensitive subject binding
hypothesis: A named subject should prevent disclosure of another subject's private data.
mechanism: Require all informative non-category query terms inside each sensitive source.
limitation: Descriptive query words and aliases can cause false abstention.

name: Exact sensitive value match
hypothesis: A query containing a sensitive literal should not retrieve different values.
mechanism: Require every supplied sensitive literal to occur in the original source.
limitation: Only recognized literals are gated; unquoted credential punctuation is literal.

name: Source privacy marker
hypothesis: Explicit non-disclosure wording should block that source from retrieval.
mechanism: Remove source text marked private, confidential, or not for sharing.
limitation: A quoted or historical discussion of privacy wording can be over-filtered.

name: Minimum supported sentence
hypothesis: A matched sentence discloses less than a full chunk containing private data.
mechanism: Emit the shortest original sentence covering every informative query term.
limitation: Paraphrases cause abstention; original context metadata is retained unchanged.

name: Asserted evidence or abstention
hypothesis: Questions, hypotheticals, and stated unknowns should not be treated as facts.
mechanism: Emit exact query-supporting assertions; return nothing if none are present.
limitation: Lexical assertion rules miss indirect evidence and can reject modal facts.
